sentences.text: The petitioner has filed the present petition, inter alia, praying that respondents be directed not to take possession of land measuring 741 square meters falling in Khasra no.271/2 located in the revenue estate in the village Rangpuri.
2. The controversy raised by the petitioner centres around land comprising in Khasra No.271 in the revenue estate of village Rangpuri.
The petitioner states that originally the said land measured 3 bighas and 15 biswas and the petitioner's father Sh. Jeet Ram son of Kanhaiya was the recorded owner of the said land.
However, a part of the said land was acquired pursuant to a notification issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereafter the LA Act).

sentences.text: The petitioner states that in terms of the said Award, 2 bighas and 2 biswas of land (out of total land of 3 bighas and 15 biswas) was acquired for the purposes of construction of road linking Palam diversion Gurgaon Bypass.
The petitioner submits that the land comprising in Khasra No.271/1 was divided into two parts being 271/1 measuring 271min. and 271/2.
The first part, that is, 271/1 measuring 2 bighas and 2 biswas was acquired on 30.12.1988.
The petitioner states that the possession of the said land was also taken over on 05.09.1986 in terms of the possession report dated 05.09.1986.
There is some controversy with regard to the same as the learned counsel for the LAC states that the possession of the said land was taken over on 02.04.1987.
However, it is not disputed that possession of the acquired land being 2 bighas and 2 biswas being a part of the land comprising Khasra No.271 was taken over.
4. The remaining land measuring 1 bigha and 13 biswas (Khasra no.271/2) continued to remain with the petitioner.
The area of the said land corresponds to 1664 square yards or 1391 square meters.
The petitioner claims that he is operating petrol pump on the part of the said land.
5. The part of the said lands measuring 650 square meters (out of 1391 square meters) was acquired in terms of an award dated 18.12.2018 (Award no.2/2018/NHAI).
In view of the above, the petitioner claims that he was left with the balance land admeasuring 741 square meters (which translates to 17 biswas and 12 biswansi).
6. The petitioner contends that in the process of taking over possession of 650 square meters, the National Highway Authority of India (hereafter This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/02/2025 at 00:59:55 NHAI) has also taken over possession of a part of the remaining lands (741 square meters) which according to the petitioner remained out of the total 1391 square meters comprising in Khasra No.271/2.
7.
The petitioner states that in view of the aforesaid, he had filed a representation dated 20.08.2020 for a fresh demarcation of the subject land.
The petitioner states that thereafter, a demarcation of the land was carried out by the Tehsildar and a report dated 21.10.2020 was furnished.
The said report suggests that possession of excess land has been taken over by NHAI.
8. However, NHAI disputes that possession of any excess land has been taken over.
Insofar as the 650 square meters of land, which was acquired, an award has already been passed by the Competent Authority for Land Acquisition (CALA).

9. It is apparent from the above that the controversy is narrowed down to the possession of 741 square meters of land, which continues to be owned by the petitioner after the two tranches of acquisition.
The first which comprised of 2 bighas and 2 biswas and the second of 650 square meters.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid, it was suggested by Mr Pathak, the learned counsel appearing for LAC that a fresh demarcation exercise be conducted by adoption of a Total Station Method (TSM).

The said suggestion was noted in the order dated 14.11.2024 and proceedings were deferred for the petitioner to obtain instructions as to whether the petitioner would bear the cost of the said exercise.
11.
The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submits that at the first instance, the petitioner would bear the cost of conducting the demarcation exercise by TSM.
However, he requests that in the event it is found that the respondent authorities have taken over possession in excess of
This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 15/02/2025 at 00:59:55 what has been acquired by them, the said cost should be reimbursed by them.
We find the said suggestion reasonable and justified.
Clearly, the petitioner cannot be called upon to bear the cost of demarcation if its claim that the possession of excess land has been taken over is found to be correct.

12. In view of the above, we direct the concerned SDM to take immediate steps for conducting the demarcation exercise through TSM, the SDM shall inform the petitioner as to the cost to be deposited for such exercise.

The petitioner shall immediately, on being informed of the same,
deposit the same with the concerned authorities.
13. We direct that the demarcation exercise be completed as expeditiously as possible and preferably within a period of six months from date.

As stated above, in the event it is found that NHAI or the concerned authorities are in possession of land in excess of what has been acquired, the concerned respondent is at liberty to take further steps accordingly.
14. All rights and contentions of the parties, including the right of the petitioner to claim damages and/or compensation, are reserved.
The petitioner would depending on results of the demarcation exercise, be at liberty to avail of appropriate remedies.
15. The petition is disposed of with the aforesaid directions.
The pending application is also disposed of.
